method: Located C&EN's own ACS Spring 2025 (San Diego) meeting-program PDF via one web search for the C&EN filename pattern (cen.acs.org/.../meeting-program.pdf), then fetched the PDF myself this session with curl and extracted text with `pdftotext -layout`. The programme itself states, on the page reproduced at grep line ~64-65 of the extracted text: '12,723 accepted papers, including 6,736 in-person oral presentations and 941 digital oral presentations' and '5,046 poster presentations, including 1,041 Sci-Mix presentations.' 6,736+941+5,046=12,723, confirming internal consistency. Invited/plenary/keynote sessions are not part of this accepted-papers figure (it is explicitly the oral+poster count). No attendance figure appears in this PDF (checked via grep for attend/registrant/participant) so attendance is left null rather than guessed. English only searched (US-based ACS, no local-language pass needed).

conference: ASMS Annual Conference on Mass Spectrometry and Allied Topics
method: One search located the ASMS 2025 business-meeting slide deck (asms.org 'ASMS Meeting_Final_presented-June-4-2025.pdf'). Fetched it myself with curl and extracted with pdftotext -layout. Its 'Program Data' 5-year table (2021-2025, Philadelphia/Minneapolis/Houston/Anaheim/Baltimore) gives, for 2025 (Baltimore): Abstracts submitted 3,586; Invited 4 plenaries + 2 tutorials (excluded, not contributed); Orals 384; Posters (in-person) 2,968. Reported abstracts_numeric = Orals + Posters = 384 + 2,968 = 3,352 (accepted contributed presentations only, excluding the 234 submitted-but-not-presented/invited difference from the 3,586 submitted figure). Attendance: same search surfaced the 73rd ASMS 2025 exhibitor prospectus PDF (already in hand, no extra search), which states on p.1 'we expect an attendance of 6,500 scientists and 3,000 talks and posters' -- an A1-rung projected exhibitor-prospectus figure, UNSPECIFIED basis. English only (US society, no local-language pass needed).

3 searches used (cap reached), none of which by itself yielded an abstracts figure I could verify by opening the source page (rule: never write down a figure only seen in a snippet). Tried: (1) aiche.org/conferences/aiche-annual-meeting/2025 -- Cloudflare JS challenge, both curl (spoofed UA) and WebFetch returned the challenge page / 403, so the page itself could not be read. (2) The official 2025 full technical-program PDF (aiche.org/.../9952_25_ann25_pb_press_20251027.pdf, fetched directly, no search) is a session GRID (session number, title, day/time/room) -- it lists ~800+ sessions but never lists individual papers/abstracts per session, so it is not a countable artefact for an abstract count (confirmed by reading it: grep for a stated total found nothing). (3) Tried AIChE's Confex backing API per the method's rung-4 pattern (aiche.confex.com/aiche/2025/meetingapi.cgi/Program) -- it returns 200 and valid JSON, but the ChildList_Paper/ChildList_Session arrays are empty at every level I could query (top-level and per-track), so this deployment does not expose the paper tree the way AcademyHealth's did. (4) proceedings.aiche.org (the paper-index site named in the chemistry field notes) is behind the same Cloudflare challenge via curl/WebFetch. A snippet-only 'AIChE: over 760 sessions and ~6,000 papers (2024), ~5,200 papers (2023)' surfaced across two searches but I never located and opened the actual AIChE page stating those totals (chenected.aiche.org/2025/01/2024-aiche-annual-meeting-recap, which I did open, states only '700+ technical sessions' for 2024, no paper/abstract total), so per rule 3 / rule 7 of the method I am not recording the 6,000/5,200 figures. Attendance IS confirmed by opening a real page: chenected.aiche.org 2024 recap states 'Participation at the 2024 AIChE Annual Meeting ... topped 5,800' (UNSPECIFIED basis). English only searched (US society; no local-language pass applicable). NEXT ACTION: rung 5 -- open aiche.confex.com/aiche/2025 webprogram (or proceedings.aiche.org) with a real browser (Playwright/Chrome), which the method notes defeats Cloudflare/JS walls that beat curl and WebFetch, and either export or count the individual paper listing directly.

conference: GDCh Wissenschaftsforum Chemie (WiFo) / Science Forum Chemistry
method: Searched in German (mandatory local-language pass, society is German/GDCh): 'Anzahl Beitraege Vortraege Poster Teilnehmer', 'Nachrichten aus der Chemie ... Teilnehmer Vortraege Poster Rueckblick Leipzig 2023', 'Teilnehmerinnen und Teilnehmer OR Besucherinnen und Besucher Leipzig Anzahl' -- 3 searches, cap reached. Every search's auto-summary asserted 'knapp 1.200 Besucherinnen und Besucher' (nearly 1,200 attendees) for WiFo 2023 Leipzig, but I could not locate and open the actual page stating it: gdch.de's own WiFo pages (wifo-2019.html, wifo-2023.html) are Next.js SPA shells that return only CSS/JSON scaffolding to curl with no rendered article text (confirmed by grepping the raw HTML for '1200'/'1.200'/'Besucher' -- zero matches in either 196KB file). I also opened chemieproduktion-online.de, idw-online.de/de/event73040, verbaende.com, chemistryviews.org and tu-dresden.de directly (zero extra search cost) and none of them contains the figure either. archive.org/wayback was rate-limited (429) both times I tried it. Per the method's rule against writing down a search-snippet-only figure, I am NOT recording the ~1,200 attendance figure or any abstracts figure, even though it recurred across independent searches, because I never actually read it on an opened page myself this session. No abstracts/Beitraege count was even suggested by any search. NEXT ACTION: rung 5 -- render gdch.de's WiFo page (or the GDCh.app event page at gdch.app/event/gdch-wissenschaftsforum-chemie-2023) with a real browser so the Next.js content actually loads, or retry web.archive.org once its rate limit clears.

3 searches used (cap reached: (1) generic abstracts-submitted query, (2) 'book of abstracts filetype:pdf', (3) total-abstracts/participants query). None gave a directly citable total, but search 2/3 surfaced europacat2023.cz, which I opened myself and found links to 'Book of abstracts' and 'Statistics from the congress'. Downloaded the actual Book of Abstracts PDF (europacat2023.cz/.../Book_of_abstracts-EuropaCat2023.pdf) directly -- 1,863 pages, 548MB, confirmed genuine via title/committee pages. Extracted full text with pdftotext -raw (splitting on form-feed chars, one array element per page). Classified every page programmatically by its first line: 'ad' if it carries the Parr Instrument Company exhibitor boilerplate (22 pages), 'frontmatter' for the first 5 title/committee/sponsor pages, 'continuation' if the first line is 'References', 'Acknowledgments', a numbered citation '[n]'/'n.', a horizontal rule, or begins with a lowercase letter (mid-sentence carry-over from the previous page) -- 187+17=204 pages, and everything else as 'abstract_start' (a fresh Title-Case abstract heading) -- 1,602 pages. Manually walked pages 8-43 (the section between the front matter and the first plainly-contributed research abstract on p.44) and counted 32 invited items there (7 Plenary lectures pp.8-14, 22 Keynote lectures pp.16-37 incl. one under a 'General Business' session label, plus an AI-authored keynote and the EFCATS Best PhD Thesis Award talk on pp.39-42) -- all excluded as invited/non-contributed. Contributed abstracts = 1,602 - 32 = 1,570 (orals+posters combined; the book does not separate them typographically, so this is a joint total, not split). This is a page-census derived count, not a clean unique-ID grep (no ID scheme is printed in this book), so confidence is 'derived' rather than 'exact' -- spot-checked because the figure lands close to the 1,500 VERIFIED line: reviewed pages 44-120 by hand (sampled every ~10 pages) and confirmed every one is a normal single-author-block contributed abstract, no further invited talks bleeding into that range. Attendance: europacat2023.cz's own welcome/call-for-papers text (opened directly, not a snippet) states 'We expect that the conference will attract over 1 500 participants' -- a pre-event PROJECTED figure (A1-type, UNSPECIFIED basis), not a post-meeting report; the site's separate 'Statistics from the congress' page is a video, not text, and was not opened. English only searched (Czech Republic host, but EFCATS/EuropaCat operates in English; no local-language pass needed for this pan-European federation event).

Searched in German (DECHEMA/ACHEMA is a German trade fair+congress): 'Anzahl wissenschaftliche Vortraege Kongressbeitraege...', 'Call for Papers Abstract Einreichung wissenschaftliche Beitraege Auswahl', 'eingereichte Beitraege angenommen Vortraege ohne Workshops' -- 3 searches, cap reached. Confirmed the ACHEMA Congress does run a genuine open Call for Papers (achema.de/en/press/press-releases/article/achema-2024-call-for-papers-for-the-achema-congress-opens: abstract max 3,000 characters, program committee accepts/rejects), so it is not purely curated -- character judged HYBRID (part open-call contributed talks, part invited Highlight Sessions / Innovation Stages). Opened the actual chemie.de Abschlussbericht (post-event report) page myself and confirmed the direct quote: 'das hochkaraetige und breite ACHEMA-Kongressprogramm mit ueber 900 Vortraegen, Diskussionsrunden und Workshops' (over 900 lectures, discussion rounds AND workshops -- combined, not separable) and 'mehr als 30.000 Zuhoerer' (30,000+ congress listeners, separate from the 106,001 total trade-fair attendees). No source found that splits the 900 figure into pure accepted-abstract oral talks vs. panel discussions vs. workshops, and ACHEMA's congress format has no poster session at all (it is talks-only), so I cannot report an 'orals+posters' figure per the task's definition -- recording UNKNOWN rather than using the conflated 900 number. NEXT ACTION: rung 4 -- open achema.de's own congress-programme archive (achema.de/de/die-achema/kongressprogramm) or the session-by-session programme PDF, which should let a session-type (Vortrag vs Workshop vs Diskussionsrunde) breakdown be counted directly at zero search cost.

conference: Keystone Symposia on Molecular and Cellular Biology
method: 2 searches: (1) confirmed format -- Keystone Symposia's own 'Submit an Abstract'/'Speaker Abstract Submission Guidelines' pages show it is NOT a pure open-call conference: main talks are by invited speakers, and only poster space (and occasionally a short oral slot pulled from posters) is opened to submitted abstracts, so the abstract pool per meeting is a minority of attendees, not the whole audience. (2) searched for typical individual-meeting size; found and opened en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keystone_Symposia myself, which states the organization 'has hosted approximately 1,600 meetings with 500,000 attendees' -- an average of ~312 attendees per individual meeting (500,000/1,600), a real sourced figure I read directly on the page, not a snippet. 'Keystone Symposia on Molecular and Cellular Biology' is the name of the whole organization/series (it runs dozens of differently-themed, separately-registered meetings per year, each capped small by design -- 'small, retreat-style settings' per keystonesymposia.org/conferences/why-participate), so this row, AS NAMED, represents one typical/representative meeting rather than a single mega-congress. Rung 9 conversion: even at a generous ~90% abstract-to-attendee ratio for a small poster-heavy invite-led meeting (chemistry biology-adjacent meetings run high per the field notes), 312 x 0.9 = 281, nowhere near the ~900 floor (flexing the ratio to 200% of an average meeting's attendance -- i.e., assuming the row instead means the single largest Keystone meeting in this series -- would need >3x the mean to reach the floor, for which no evidence exists). This matches the chemistry field notes verbatim: 'Individually they fail the bar; collectively they would swing the headline conference count' for Keystone/GRC/CECAM/Telluride-type invite-led series. OPEN QUESTION FLAGGED (per field notes, not resolved here): whether this should be one row (as censused here, OUT) or split into many rows aggregating the whole series -- that decision is Rupert's, not mine.
